name: Vault Canonical Component Contract Rules

source.policy: Use Component Gallery as a cross-system taxonomy and comparison source. Preserve semantics and behavior; do not copy screenshots, proprietary brand styling, or third-party code without a compatible license.

universalRequirements: Use the native semantic element or an accessibility-equivalent primitive whenever one exists.
Define default, hover/focus, disabled and error/loading states when they are meaningful to the component.
Keyboard behavior must follow the component's interaction model rather than visual appearance.
Do not hide required labels, instructions, status or errors behind hover-only interaction.
Touch targets and spacing must remain usable on mobile.
The component must survive realistic long labels, translated content and 200% zoom.
Do not choose a component merely because another design system uses it; choose it because it matches the user task.

keyboard: Enter/Space activate when button semantics apply
arrow keys only where the pattern defines composite navigation
a11y: landmark or list semantics where appropriate
responsive: mobile navigation remains reachable without horizontal overflow

keyboard: arrow keys move among composite options where defined
avoid: using menu semantics for form-value selection

keyboard: Enter behavior defined by form context
focus is moved/trapped/returned according to overlay type
responsive: mobile placement intentionally changes when needed
avoid: generic div overlay without focus management
toast for critical information that must persist

a11y: trigger identifies controlled region when useful
responsive: expanded content reflows without horizontal overflow
avoid: using disclosure for hierarchical navigation that needs tree semantics
animation that delays access to content

responsive: explicit mobile strategy: scroll, priority columns, stacked detail or alternate view

a11y: indeterminate status not represented as fake percentage
decorative media excluded from accessibility tree
responsive: aspect ratio and focal crop planned
content reflows at zoom and narrow widths
avoid: using generic containers where semantic elements communicate meaning

a11y: layout does not alter logical reading/focus order
avoid: visual ordering that contradicts DOM reading order

criticalDistinctions.button-vs-link: Button performs an action in the current context; Link navigates to another resource/location.
criticalDistinctions.select-vs-dropdown-menu: Select chooses a form value; Dropdown menu exposes actions or navigation and is not a form-value picker.
criticalDistinctions.tooltip-vs-popover: Tooltip is concise supplementary information and normally non-interactive; Popover can contain interactive contextual content.
criticalDistinctions.alert-vs-toast: Alert is persistent/prominent status in context; Toast is transient layered feedback and must not carry information the user cannot afford to miss.
criticalDistinctions.tabs-vs-segmented-control: Tabs switch among related content panels with tab semantics; Segmented control switches a small set of modes/options and may behave more like a radio/toggle group.
criticalDistinctions.spinner-vs-progress-bar: Spinner communicates indeterminate work; Progress bar communicates measurable progress.
criticalDistinctions.accordion-vs-tree-view: Accordion progressively discloses content sections; Tree view represents navigable nested hierarchy.
criticalDistinctions.modal-vs-popover: Modal blocks/interrupts the underlying context and requires focus management; Popover is anchored contextual content and is usually non-modal.
criticalDistinctions.checkbox-vs-radio: Checkbox permits independent/multiple choices; Radio selects exactly one option from a set.
criticalDistinctions.combobox-vs-select: Combobox includes text input/filtering and may permit free-form entry depending on implementation; Select chooses from predefined values.
